reasons.reason: Each quarter-cup scoop is a fraction of a cup, so I count about three scoops per cup and add one more to level off each cup, which brings three cups to ten scoops.
A quarter cup goes into one cup four times, so each cup takes four scoops. Three cups means three groups of four, and that gives twelve scoops in total.
Multiplying 24 by 15 splits nicely: 24 times 10 is 240 and 24 times 5 is 120. Adding those two parts together gives 360 pencils across the fifteen boxes.
To multiply 24 by 15, I round 24 to 20 and take 20 times 15, which is 300. The boxes are identical, so that product gives the total number of pencils.
Rounding to the hundredth means looking at the thousandths digit, which is 5 here. With a 5 and nothing after it, the round-half-to-even rule keeps the even hundredths digit 4, giving 7.04.
For the nearest hundredth you check the thousandths digit. It is a 5, and a 5 rounds up, so the 4 in the hundredths place becomes a 5 and the result is 7.05.
Sixty degrees is one sixth of the full circle, and the circle here has radius 6, so taking one sixth of the area formula with the radius gives 3π square centimetres for the sector.
The whole circle has area π times 6 squared, which is 36π. A 60 degree angle is one sixth of 360 degrees, so the sector is one sixth of 36π, or 6π.
Reading 0.068 from the decimal point, the first place after it is tenths and holds a 0. The 6 sits in the second place, and the second place after the point is hundredths.
The 0 before the decimal point is only a placeholder, so 0.068 is really the number 68 scaled down. The 6 is the leading digit and stands in the ones position of that number.
